leads.posting: Pre-owned goods marketplace Circle raises Rs 25 Cr led by Nexus Venture Partners. Bengaluru based pre-owned goods marketplace Circle has raised Rs 25 crore in a seed funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners. Existing investor Titan Capital and Myntra co-founder Raveen Sastry also participated in the round, along with Delhivery COO Ajith Pai as an angel investor. The fresh capital will be used to expand beyond Bengaluru and strengthen the company’s AI-based pricing, product discovery and verification capabilities. Circle also plans to expand its Trust Hubs and logistics network as it scales operations across India. Founded in 2025 by Chirag Kataruka and Ankit Misra, Circle operates a managed customer-to-customer (C2C) marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned products. Its platform combines AI-based technology, product verification and logistics to facilitate transactions without owning inventory. Within a year of launch, Circle claims to have facilitated around Rs 25 crore in pre-owned sales. The platform has attracted over 10 lakh visitors and generated 1 lakh listings in Bengaluru. According to the company, sellers typically find buyers within three days. Nearly 40% of its buyers return within 90 days, while half of its sellers list products again. Circle offers products across categories including smartphones, gaming consoles, cameras, furniture, watches, handbags and sneakers. Its services include product verification, pickup, payments and a three-day Circle Guarantee for buyers.

leads.posting: The Pant Project raises Rs 109 Cr in Series B led by Mirae Asset. Premium menswear brand The Pant Project has raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments (India), with participation from existing investor Sorin Investments and new investors Hyperscale Ventures, B&K Securities, MGA Ventures and B2V Ventures, as per the company’s press release. The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its offline retail network, enter new product categories and strengthen its omnichannel presence. Founded by brothers Dhruv and Udit Toshniwal, The Pant Project started as a digital-first brand focused on bottomwear for Indian men. Its product portfolio includes Malai Pants and Inklock No Fade Black Jeans. The company currently operates 25 exclusive brand stores across India and plans to increase the count to over 150 in the next two to three years. It also plans to expand into adjacent menswear categories, including jeans, athleisure and casualwear. Commenting on the fundraise, Dhruv Toshniwal, founder and CEO of The Pant Project, said the company is now looking to expand its offline presence after building its business as a digital-first brand. He said its stores allow customers to experience the fabric and fit of its products in person, helping the company build stronger relationships with customers. The latest fundraising follows its $4.25 million Series A round in 2024, led by Sorin Investments. The company had bootstrapped its business before raising institutional capital. Alongside the equity round, The Pant Project has also secured venture debt financing from Alteria Capital, although the amount was not disclosed. IndigoEdge acted as the investment banker for the Series B transaction. The fresh capital will help the company scale its retail network and broaden its product portfolio as it looks to build a larger presence in India’s premium menswear market.

leads.posting: Hunar Raises ₹40 Cr To Scale Agentic AI For Frontline Hiring. Hiring thousands of frontline workers (employees who directly provide goods and services to communities) across multiple cities is a coordination-heavy cumbersome task for HR managers. Recruiters have to call prospective employees, follow up on applications, schedule interviews and keep workers informed through onboarding and training. When hiring volumes spike during festive seasons or business expansion, these tasks can quickly become more difficult to solve manually. Bengaluru-based conversational AI startup Hunar.AI is building AI agents to automate these HR workflows. The startup today announced the raise of ₹40 Cr ($4.2 Mn) in its Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. Other investors like Hyderabad Angels Fund, Together Fund, Seedstars, AVNM Ventures, PhysicsWallah cofounders Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey, and MediaMint cofounder Aditya Vuchi also participated in the round. Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar.AI automates frontline workforce management via its conversational AI agents. These agents help ease various frontline workforce management issues — including hiring, onboarding, training and retention. It is targeting businesses that need to recruit and manage large numbers of workers, often across several locations and regional languages. The startup offers voice AI capabilities in more than 20 languages, including Tamil, Telugu and Kannada. This allows enterprises to communicate with workers in their preferred languages while automating workflows that would otherwise require repeated calls and manual follow-ups. The startup intends to use the fresh capital to strengthen its AI infrastructure, develop its products and bolster its go-to-market strategy. “Frontline workforce management is one of the largest yet most underserved opportunities in enterprise AI.
